title: Trevor Lawrence bolsters MVP case, Jaguars’ AFC credentials with lights-out day vs. Titans
content:
The Jacksonville Jaguars didn’t use two of their biggest trade-deadline acquisitions Sunday but still rolled to a 40-23 road victory over the Tennessee Titans.

Trevor Lawrence threw for 352 yards and three touchdowns, further solidifying his standing as a fringe MVP candidate. His lone turnover, a first-quarter interception, came on a ball that was tipped at the line of scrimmage. Top receiver Parker Washington had 152 receiving yards, 148 of them coming in a huge first half.

The Titans hung in, staying within 7 points of the Jaguars in the fourth quarter. Playing without No. 1 receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder), Cam Ward threw for 231 yards, two touchdowns and an interception.

The Jaguars did not play their two biggest trade-deadline acquisitions, defensive tackle Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates III, both of whom were inactive Sunday. On Friday, head coach Liam Coen explained that since neither player had a bye week with their former teams, Jacksonville would hold them back this week rather than have them play an 18-game season. (The Jaguars had their bye in Week 7.) Jacksonville’s other deadline acquisition, DT Davon Godchaux, had his bye week with the New Orleans Saints and played against the Titans.

Box score | Week 10 live blog | Game discussion

The Jaguars’ defense has been the talk of the league this past week, as they went hard in upgrading the unit at the trade deadline. With Davis and Bates sitting out Sunday, we’ll have to wait and see how the new-look Jaguars defense looks in the coming weeks.

Instead, this game was a reminder that the offense shouldn’t be taken lightly.

Jacksonville might not have name-brand star power, but they are solid at every position and have great depth. Washington is the No. 1 receiver, but Jakobi Meyers has shown that kind of ability, too. Despite playing through injuries, running back Bhayshul Tuten is having a breakout season, and Chris Rodriguez gives the team a dependable backup.

Tight end Brenton Strange produces in the pass game, but Nate Boerkircher shows up, too.

Of course, Lawrence makes the whole operation work. Ever since Coen’s arrival, Lawrence has been phenomenal and, as silly as it may seem given his pre-draft hype, may be one of the more underrated quarterbacks in the NFL.

The quarterback decision is going to be an interesting one for the Titans. It wasn’t long ago that head coach Robert Saleh had to answer questions about Ward’s effectiveness, and even explain why the second-year quarterback wasn’t benched.

However, Ward’s full body of work this season does offer encouraging signs. Ward hasn’t been consistent but has flashed the kind of potential that made him the top pick of the 2025 draft. The Titans must do an honest evaluation of Ward and determine if there’s enough to build around him, or if Ward is the issue.

The Titans don’t have a great set of weapons and were without Tate on Sunday. Given the investment of a No. 1 pick, it would be surprising if Tennessee decided to move on regardless of how high its draft slot is in 2027. The Panthers with Bryce Young don’t offer an exact parallel but could offer a blueprint for letting a top draft pick work through his rookie contract and see if he can iron out the inconsistencies as he gains more experience and the talent around him improves.

It’s not an outlandish claim. Washington doesn’t put up big numbers like other elite receivers around the league, but that’s not really his fault. The Jaguars have been one of the NFL’s most complete teams — offense, defense and special teams — this season, which has led to some dominating wins. Coming into Week 10, four of their six wins were by at least 23 points. As a result, Jacksonville hasn’t had to throw it much in the second half. In fact, the Jaguars often don’t even have to play their starters late.

Sunday’s game against the Titans was close throughout, and Washington was involved early and often. Of course, the Titans defense was picked over at the trade deadline, with top playmakers like DT Jeffery Simmons (traded to Chicago) and safety Amani Hooker (Buffalo) no longer around. But Washington has shown an ability to produce against better competition, too. He isn’t in the top tier of NFL receivers (with the likes of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, CeeDee Lamb and Ja’Marr Chase), but he’s in the next tier down.
